I love sports and had been a swimmer too, so I decided to switch to para-athletics. This is how my Paralympics journey began. My breakthrough moment came in the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games, when I secured the silver medal in the shot-put event. In hindsight, I feel it was a moment of personal victory and a step forward in changing perceptions.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding a disability sports awareness and advocacy session for all students, and the Sports Captain has been asked to announce it. Write a notice of 100 words for the school notice board, giving the purpose of the session and inviting students to attend.

markingPoints.description: Gives the notice a clear heading naming the awareness and advocacy session
States the purpose of the session and says who will be speaking at it
Invites the students to attend and tells them what to expect or bring
Uses the layout of a notice — short clear blocks with the key details, and no unnecessary sentences
Uses accurate spelling, grammar and punctuation, and stays within 100 words

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
NOTICE

Disability Sports Awareness and Advocacy Session

Our school is holding a session on disability sports for all students. Para-athletes will speak about how sport has given them a new lease of life and helped them push boundaries. The session will also show how disability is not a limitation but a unique strength waiting to be unleashed.

All students are welcome to attend. Come with your questions, and be ready to think about ability beyond disability. Students who attend will also learn how they can support para sportspersons in their own neighbourhood.

Sports Captain

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding an assembly on the theme “Ability Beyond Disability”. Write a speech of 100 words for your classmates in which you explain what watching para-athletes does to people’s thinking, and then suggest two things your audience can do.

markingPoints.description: Greets the audience and states the theme of the speech in the opening lines
Explains what watching para-athletes does to people’s thinking
Gives at least two clear suggestions for what the audience can do
Keeps a clear order — opening, main points and conclusion — joined by linking words such as “so” and “and”
Uses accurate spelling, grammar and punctuation with a suitable speaking style, within 100 words

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Good morning everyone. Today I want to talk about ability, not about disability.

When people watch the strength, skill and competitive spirit of para-athletes, it breaks down preconceived notions. Sport gives them a new lease of life and helps them push boundaries. Individuals with disabilities can be as capable, if not more than their able-bodied counterparts.

So what can we do? We can treat every person with dignity and give them a fair chance to succeed. We can attend a disability sports awareness session in our own school. And we can remember that every setback is an opportunity to prove your strength.

Thank you.

questions.stem: You and your classmates want to collect sports equipment for para sportspersons in your area. Write an e-mail of 100 words to the Principal explaining who the equipment is for, how you plan to collect it, and why the effort is worth making.

markingPoints.description: Begins with a suitable greeting and states the purpose of the e-mail in the opening lines
Explains who the equipment is for and why they may not be able to buy it
Lists the practical steps the students will take to collect and check the equipment
Closes with a polite request and sign-off, keeping a clear logical order
Uses accurate spelling, grammar and punctuation, and stays within 100 words

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Principal,

With your permission, I and my classmates would like to collect sports equipment for para sportspersons in our area. Many of them train hard but cannot easily afford the gear they need, so a gift of used equipment would mean a great deal to them.

We plan to ask our parents, our neighbours and the local shops to donate bats, balls, gloves and skipping ropes. We will sort and check everything before handing it over, and we will tell you how much we have collected.

We believe youth is the voice of tomorrow, and every sportsperson deserves a fair chance to compete.

Yours sincerely,
A student of your school

questions.stem: A classmate is asked to explain how Dr. Deepa Malik moved from a spine tumour to a Paralympic silver medal. Set out, step by step, the stages of that journey in the order in which they happened.

markingPoints.description: At 29 she was diagnosed with a spine tumour and underwent a surgery
The doctors declared she would be bound to a wheelchair for the rest of her life, as she was paralysed waist down
She chose to transform her life into a world of limitless possibilities instead of squandering it in remorse
Since she loved sports and had been a swimmer, she switched to para-athletics
The support of her family, coupled with her fortitude, turned obstacles into stepping stones
Her breakthrough came at the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games, where she secured the silver medal in the shot-put event

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. At 29 she was diagnosed with a spine tumour and underwent a surgery.
2. Misfortune followed: the doctors declared she would be bound to a wheelchair for the rest of her life, as she was paralysed waist down.
3. She chose not to squander her life in remorse, but to transform it into a world of limitless possibilities.
4. Since she loved sports and had been a swimmer, she switched to para-athletics; this was where her Paralympics journey began.
5. The support of her family, coupled with her own fortitude, turned obstacles into stepping stones.
6. Her breakthrough came at the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games, where she secured the silver medal in the shot-put event.
